Synopsis:
NY Fed Q2 household debt report shows record nominal auto loan originations ($211B), rising HELOC/credit card balances, but overall debt dipped to $18.8T due to a mortgage reporting technicality. Delinquency rates edged down to 4.7%; credit card delinquency is elevated but stable since 2024, with the apparent deterioration explained by lenders holding stale charged-off debt longer — not a fundamental worsening. Consumer spending rebounded sharply (PCE +3.2% Q2), BofA July card data shows continued solid spending, and household financial health broadly remains resilient despite real income pressure.
